title: Zion’s redemption waits for a prepared, endowed people
setting: Joseph Smith led an armed expedition, later called Zion’s Camp, from Ohio to Missouri in May and June 1834. It aimed to help Saints driven from Jackson County regain their lands. Governor Daniel Dunklin did not call out the militia to escort them, and a Clay County delegation warned of violence. On 22 June 1834, at a campsite about four miles north of Fishing River, Joseph dictated this revelation. Soon after, the camp disbanded, and cholera struck many members.
summary: The revelation, addressed to those gathered, says Zion could have been redeemed already but for the church’s transgressions. It names disobedience, failure to share with the poor, and lack of union, mainly among the churches abroad. It says the elders must wait “for a little season” and first be “endowed with power from on high”. That endowment is to come in the house being built in Kirtland. It says the Lord will fight Zion’s battles and accepts the offering of those who came. Those who can stay in the region should stay; those with families in the east are to follow Joseph’s direction. The Saints are to buy land in Jackson County and nearby counties, gather quietly, and not boast. It closes by telling them to “sue for peace” with all people.

contextNote.title: Waiting as a season of preparation
contextNote.text: The camp had marched hundreds of miles and now would not enter Jackson County. Verse 9 says the elders must wait for Zion’s redemption. Verse 10 gives the reason: so they may be prepared and taught more perfectly. Verse 11 adds that this cannot happen until they are “endowed with power from on high”. Verse 33 places that endowment in the house commanded in Kirtland. Verses 3–4 explain why preparation was lacking: the Saints were not united and did not care for the poor. In this passage, waiting means a season of training before Zion’s redemption is pursued again.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 102–105 presents Zion’s Camp as a trial that prepared faithful disciples. What do verses 3–6 suggest about the kind of people who can build Zion?
reviewNote: Read all 41 verses. Official heading gives 22 June 1834, about four miles north of Fishing River, Clay County, Missouri, after the governor declined to call out the militia. JSP introduction read for the camp size, the Clay County delegation led by Sheriff Cornelius Gilliam, the campsite on John Cooper’s property, the disbanding, and cholera. JSP says Dunklin seemed reluctant rather than formally refusing; setting says he did not call out the militia. independence is used to stand for Jackson County (vv. 28, and setting). Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary now says those with families in the east are to follow Joseph's direction (v. 21 says 'tarry'; it does not say 'return'); Lord's promise attributed to the revelation.
